title: The Daily Out-Load Ceiling the Facility Works To
content:
The ceiling on a release is what the facility can work in a day. This rule governs releases out of store under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements and turns on the house the grain is held at and on recent out-load work on the agreement.

## Standing rule

Where the grain is held at a rail terminal and no load-out has been worked on the agreement in the last thirty days, the rail ceiling of 28000 bushels applies.

Where the grain is held at a rail terminal and a load-out has been worked on the agreement in the last thirty days, the reduced rail ceiling of 14000 bushels applies, the elevator spreading its out-load capacity across its members.

And otherwise the country ceiling of 12000 bushels applies.

## Which houses are rail terminals

The cooperative's rail terminals are the Kellerton Rail Terminal and the Winnebago River Terminal. Grain held at the Prairie Ridge Main Elevator, the Ash Grove Annex or the Bergen Siding Elevator is not held at a rail terminal.

## Truth table of the conditions

| The house the grain is held at | A load-out worked on the agreement in the last thirty days | Ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a rail terminal | no | 28000 |
| a rail terminal | yes | 14000 |
| any other house | either way | 12000 |

At a country house the ceiling stands at 12000 bushels whether or not grain has moved recently.

## Worked ceilings, on hypothetical agreements

**Corn held at the Kellerton Rail Terminal with no load-out on the agreement for two months.** The ceiling is 28000 bushels.

**The same lot after a load-out worked eleven days ago.** The ceiling is 14000 bushels.

**Soybeans held at the Ash Grove Annex, whether or not anything has moved.** The ceiling is 12000 bushels.
